properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 27 at 12:25AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 1225 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 4
miles northeast of Cogar, moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 40 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Union City, Minco, Cogar, and Cedar Lake.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 27 at 12:23AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1223 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 11
miles southeast of Greenwood, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Garden City, Spraberry, and Saint Lawrence.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 27 at 12:08AM CDT until September 27 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1208 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Glasscock County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 26 at 6:23PM HST until September 26 at 9:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Hawaii in Hawaii County...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 618 PM HST, emergency management reported that portions of
Highway 11 remain closed in both directions due to flooding.
Locations include between Pinao Street and Kaalualu Road in
Waiohinu, as well as between Naalehu and Ninole. Kaalaiki Road
remains closed near the intersection with Highway 11 in Naalehu.
Areas of moderate rain will continue to move into southeast
portions of the Big Island over the next few hours with rainfall
rates generally 0.5 to 1 inch per hour.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hawaiian Paradise Park, Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Wood
Valley, Volcano, Pahala, Glenwood, Punaluu Beach, Kawa Flats,
Mountain View and Hawaiian Acres.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from streams, drainage ditches and low lying areas prone to
flooding.

A Flood Watch is also in effect for until 6 AM HST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 26 at 9:12PM CDT until September 28 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Des Plaines River near Gurnee affecting Lake IL County.

Des Plaines River near Russell affecting Lake IL County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Des Plaines River from US-41 in Gurnee downstream to
Townline Road in Vernon Hills, including the Gurnee gauge.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Forest land inundated near the river in
Gurnee.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 7.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The river has continued a gradual fall.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage on
Monday.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or
may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based almost entirely on observed precipitation
as little to no additional precipitation is currently expected over
the next 24 to 48 hours.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Sunday afternoon.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 26 at 8:36PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage and is
forecast to continue to rise slightly, cresting on Sunday due to an
ongoing period of northerly winds and tidal effects. River levels are
forecast to then gradually subside through Minor Flood Stage from
early through the middle of next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 2.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.9
feet on 10/17/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1130 AM EDT.

properties.description:

* WHERE...The Hudson River in Westchester, Rockland, Orange and
Putnam counties in southeastern New York...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to locally moderate tidal flooding in low lying
areas along the river around the times of high tide.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 612 AM EDT, Water levels along the Hudson River will increase
with successive high tide cycles. The worst flooding is expected
with the Saturday morning high tide.
